voiceover: Is Jesus God? Open Mark — the earliest Gospel — and watch how the room reacted. In chapter two, a paralyzed man is lowered to him, and Jesus says, 'Son, your sins are forgiven.' The scribes are stunned: 'Who can forgive sins but God alone?' They knew exactly what he was claiming. He calls himself Lord even of the Sabbath — the day God himself made holy. He speaks to a storm and the sea goes still, and the disciples ask, 'Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?' — for in the Psalms, it is the LORD who stills the sea. Then, on trial for his life, the high priest asks, 'Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?' Jesus answers, 'I am — and you will see the Son of Man at the right hand of Power, coming with the clouds of heaven.' The high priest tears his robes: 'You have heard the blasphemy.' A claim to God's own throne. And at the cross, a Roman centurion watches him die and says, 'Truly this man was the Son of God.' Forgiving sins. Lord of the Sabbath. Stilling the sea. Seated at God's right hand. This is who God alone is. Mark's Jesus is the Lord.
